**Purpose of this stage:** convert supplier and case data into comparable financial measures using an auditable spreadsheet structure.

**Outcome for this stage:** **Construct an auditable spreadsheet model that converts operational solar data into comparable Year-1 financial measures.**

**You will demonstrate this by:** calculating useful generation, gross and net Year-1 savings and simple payback; applying relative and absolute references appropriately; formatting outputs consistently; and creating a decision-relevant visual.

**Evidence:** completed `Your Model!B4:D8`{.cell}, one comparison chart and a one-sentence visual-design rationale.

Course guidance · build the comparison

## Turn three supplier proposals into one auditable model

Management needs a common basis for comparison. Build the logic in the **Your Model** sheet: useful generation → gross saving → net saving → simple payback.
::::

:::::::: card
::::::: step
::: num
1
:::

::::: content-body

### Useful generation — already started

::: formula
`Useful generation = Year-1 generation × self-consumption`
:::

**Cells:** `Your Model!B4:D4`{.cell}

**System A formula in B4:**

::: formula
`='Case Data'!B15*'Case Data'!B16`
:::

Copy `B4`{.cell} across to `D4`{.cell}. Relative references should change automatically.

:::::
:::::::
::::::::

::::::::: {.card .spaced-card}
:::::::: step
::: num
2
:::

::::: content-body

### Gross Year-1 saving

::: formula
`Gross saving = useful generation × tariff`
:::

Select `Your Model!B5`{.cell} and enter:

::: formula
`=B4*'Case Data'!$B$4`
:::

Copy across to `D5`{.cell}. The first reference changes B4 → C4 → D4; the tariff stays locked at `Case Data!$B$4`{.cell}.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Formative feedback · check values

B5 = R231,840; C5 = R287,980; D5 = R321,048.
:::

:::::
::::::::
:::::::::

::::::::: {.card .spaced-card}
:::::::: step
::: num
3
:::

::::: content-body

### Net Year-1 saving

::: formula
`Net saving = gross saving − maintenance`
:::

In `Your Model!B6`{.cell} enter:

::: formula
`=B5-'Case Data'!B17`
:::

Copy across to `D6`{.cell}. Format `B6:D6`{.cell} as rand currency.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Formative feedback · check values

B6 = R222,840; C6 = R276,980; D6 = R307,048.
:::

:::::
::::::::
:::::::::

::::::::: {.card .spaced-card}
:::::::: step
::: num
4
:::

::::: content-body

### Simple payback

::: formula
`Simple payback = installed cost ÷ Net Year-1 saving`
:::

In `Your Model!B7`{.cell} enter:

::: formula
`='Case Data'!B13/B6`
:::

Copy across to `D7`{.cell}. Format `B7:D7`{.cell} to two decimal places.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Formative feedback · diagnose your result

Your answers should be approximately A = 2.92, B = 2.96, C = 3.22 years. If not, check percentage formats, cell references, subtraction of maintenance, and numerator/denominator.
:::

:::::
::::::::
:::::::::

:::::: excel
::: label
Optional Excel skill · rank the paybacks
:::

### Use a function rather than ranking by eye

In `Your Model!B8`{.cell} enter:

::: formula
`=RANK.EQ(B7,$B$7:$D$7,1)`
:::

Copy across to `D8`{.cell}. The final argument `1`{.cell} means the smallest payback receives rank 1.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Formative feedback · check ranks

System A = 1, System B = 2, System C = 3.
:::
::::::

::::::: excel
::: label
Visual communication task
:::

### Create one chart an executive can read in five seconds

1.  Decide which single comparison your chart should communicate.
2.  For a simple-payback chart, use proposal names `B3:D3`{.cell} and payback values `B7:D7`{.cell}.

::::: platform-grid
::: platform
**Excel** Select `B3:D3`{.cell}, then add the non-adjacent `B7:D7`{.cell} range using `Ctrl`{.kbd} (Windows) or `⌘`{.kbd} (Mac). Choose **Insert → Column or Bar Chart → Clustered Column**.
:::

::: platform
**Google Sheets** The simplest beginner route is to create a small temporary two-row chart source in unused cells (for example `H3:J4`{.cell}): copy the three proposal names into row 3 and link row 4 to `B7:D7`{.cell}. Select `H3:J4`{.cell} → **Insert → Chart** → choose **Column chart** in the Chart editor. This avoids awkward non-adjacent selection.
:::
:::::

3.  Give the chart a decision-focused title such as **Simple payback by proposal**.
4.  Remove anything that does not help a manager compare the three systems.

**Write one sentence:** “I chose to show \_\_\_ because \_\_\_.”
:::::::

::: output
**Evidence produced:** completed `Your Model!B4:D8`{.cell} + one chart + one-sentence design rationale.
:::

::: next
**Next:** management challenges an assumption. Test whether your conclusion survives.
